task: Refactor the Coloring minigame around a repeatable magical-easel loop: the child starts directly on a black-and-white coloring page, asks the drawing what colour it likes, colours it freely until ROBOT POWER fills, watches the camera pull back in two stages to reveal the easel and then the whole room as the drawing hops off the page, and can walk back to the easel and start another round indefinitely. Every finished robot stays in the room forever, with its own artwork.
context: esl-likes is a five-minigame 3D ESL game for Japanese elementary classrooms (Vite + three.js), deployed live from main. Coloring is currently a one-round minigame: walk to an artist NPC in an atelier, ask it a question, hear a favourite colour, paint a robot freehand on a full-screen 2D canvas until a power bar fills, watch the robot hop off the page into the room, carry the finished picture to the artist as a gift, see it framed on the wall, answer a turnaround question, done. The owner wants that single round turned into an indefinite loop built around one central easel, with the artist NPC, the gift, the art table and the wall frame all removed, and with every robot the child creates accumulating in the room. READ .ai/coloring-easel-loop-spec.md FIRST. It is the frozen contract. It records which of the owner's requirements are ALREADY BUILT (free coloring, seven colours, three brushes, undo/eraser, the unique-area power model, the favourite-colour bonus, the connected five-piece silhouette, the hop animation, per-robot textures - do not rebuild or 'restore' any of these), the one gap in the plan that had to be closed by design (there is no way out of a minigame except finish(), which the plan deletes, and the turnaround it deletes is frozen in SPEC.md), the frozen phase list, the three camera stages, the crowd module's API, the layering trap on this screen, and the performance rules for retaining twenty robots.
requirements: Read .ai/coloring-easel-loop-spec.md first and treat it as the contract. Then read src/minigames/coloring/index.js (the whole controller), robotPuppet.js, paperPuppet.js, picture.js and coverage.js. Also read src/systems/cameraRig.js, src/systems/transitions.js and src/systems/speechPrompt.js - you are building against all three and none of them may change.

NEW src/minigames/coloring/robotCrowd.js, pure (no three.js, no DOM, no canvas), implementing the API frozen in spec section 6 exactly: createCrowd({ points, random }) with join(), leave(id) and size, where join() returns { id, start, idlePause, stateTime, points } and `points` is that member's OWN copy of the authored roam points, each displaced by one offset on a ring whose angle comes from the member index by golden angle. RING_RADIUS = 0.62 exported. A displaced point that leaves the safe area falls back to the authored point. This is the whole of the anti-pile-up mechanism: spacing is decided once at join, so there is no runtime avoidance and NOTHING THAT CAN JITTER. Do not write steering, separation forces, a navmesh or any per-frame crowd logic.

Open robotPuppet.js in exactly three places and no more: createRoamPlan(points, start, { idlePause }) takes a per-plan idlePause defaulting to the current IDLE_PAUSE constant; stepRoam reads plan.idlePause rather than the module constant; and paperPuppet.startRoaming(points, { start, idlePause, stateTime }) passes them through and seeds the initial stateTime. Existing callers and all existing tests must keep working unchanged.

Re-author OBSTACLES and ROAM_POINTS in robotPuppet.js for the new room: the art table and artist obstacles are deleted, the easel obstacle moves to the easel's new central position, and the point list grows to 8-10 points spread across the room because up to twenty robots now share it. Update the tests that pin them.

Rewrite the phase machine in index.js to exactly the phase list frozen in spec section 3. Every old phase name is deleted - approach, answer, transition-to-painting, gift, reaction, turnaround-by-artist and transition-to-room do not survive under any spelling. Do not keep a dead phase branch anywhere.

FIRST ENTRY GOES STRAIGHT TO THE PAGE. enter() builds the room, the easel and the player behind the scenes (so stage 2 and 3 have something to reveal) but starts in canvas-question with the DOM coloring screen already up and the world not visible. The child must never see the room, a walk or an easel overview before their first drawing. No walking to anything.

The DRAWING is the speaking target, not an NPC. In canvas-question the screen shows the black-and-white page and a minimal instruction, and promptQuestion() wires the HUD Talk control as it does today (it needs no 3D anchor). On acceptance the robot answers `I like ___.` through audio.speak plus a DOM SPEECH BUBBLE INSIDE THE COLORING SCREEN anchored over the canvas at the robot's head - the head occupies x 0.285-0.715, y 0.155-0.36 of the picture, so the bubble's tail sits at (0.5, 0.15) of the canvas box. dialogue.show() anchors to a 3D object and the world is hidden, so it cannot be used here. Give the drawing a small wiggle and a blink (surface.setBlink) on the same beat so it reads as the speaker. Keep the Listen Again control working and keep it counting as a replay.

TOOLS APPEAR AFTER THE ANSWER. During canvas-question the palette, the three brush buttons, the eraser, undo, the reset button and the ROBOT POWER bar are all hidden. When the answer finishes they fade/animate in together and coloring begins. No colour is preselected. Respect prefers-reduced-motion as the rest of this stylesheet already does.

Fix the layering trap recorded in spec section 9 before you test anything on this screen: .lesson-hud is z-index 20 and .coloring-screen is also z-index 20 but appended later, so the coloring screen currently paints over the HUD and the child would never see the Talk button. Move .coloring-screen to z-index 18. Verify the reset-confirm overlay and the Listen Again control are still usable.

ACTIVATION STAYS ON THE PAGE FIRST (plan section 11). At full power freeze painting input, then while still in the DOM close-up: the power bar pulses, the robot wiggles, it blinks, the body shakes, it gives one small anticipatory hop. Only then does the paper-cutout activation begin. The existing CHARGE_SECONDS beat and the coloring-wake keyframes are the starting point; extend them rather than replacing them wholesale.

THREE CAMERA STAGES, as frozen in spec section 4. Use cameraRig.setPreset with a low damping (around 2.0-2.6) for the cinematic stages and let the rig's own damping do the moving - DO NOT write a camera tween. Stage 1 frames the easel's paper tightly and must be set BEFORE the cross-fade so the 3D easel is already framed. Stage 2 pulls back to show the easel with the player standing in front of it. Stage 3 returns to the normal follow preset targeting the player.

STAGE 1 TO 2 IS A CROSS-FADE, NOT THE WIPE. Draw the finished page onto the easel's canvas texture, place the camera at stage 1, make the world visible, then fade the DOM .coloring-screen's own opacity to 0 over about 0.5 s. transitions.run() is a scale-X wipe and would break the illusion the owner is buying. The DOM canvas and the easel's paper plane must land at roughly the same screen position and size or the fade reads as two unrelated pictures - author stage 1's framing against a real screenshot and say in your report how close you got. transitions.run() is still the right tool for the to-canvas transition, which is a deliberate change of view.

THE DRAWING LEAVES THE PAGE. In robot-exit the puppet lifts off the easel's canvas, leans and peels forward, hops off the easel, drops to the floor, lands with the existing squash/bounce, and briefly celebrates. The easel's canvas MUST become blank at the moment the puppet leaves it - the same robot may never be visible both on the paper and alive at once. The wall frame and the carried-picture mesh are deleted, so there is no longer any copy of the artwork anywhere: the drawing really left.

SIMPLIFY THE ROOM (plan section 15). Delete the artist NPC (characters.create model 'b') and its picture mesh, the art table and its top, the three paint pots, the wall frame plus frameMaterial and its four wood rails, and the old off-centre easel. Keep floor, three walls, trim and lighting. Add ONE easel near the centre of the room carrying the canvas plane, and a doorway on the back wall. Nothing else. The easel must visually dominate.

THE EASEL IS THE REPLAY INTERACTION. In the room phase the player walks normally (updateMovement and canOccupy stay, with the collision shapes updated for the new layout). Near the easel, show the existing contextual action affordance and let Space start a new round through to-canvas. Space must work whether the canvas is blank, mid-fade or ready - see the next requirement - and there must be no message anywhere that tells the child to wait.

EASEL CANVAS STATES blank / fading / ready exactly as frozen in spec section 5: blank after a robot leaves, the line art fading in over about 1.2 s starting 2.5-4 s later, then ready. This is a visual invitation and NEVER a gameplay lockout. Pressing Space during blank or fading prepares the page during the to-canvas transition so the close-up is never established on an empty canvas. There is exactly ONE robot drawing - the plan's talk of generating or selecting a new picture means the fade state, not a second picture. Do not add a second picture.

THE DOOR IS THE WAY OUT, AND CARRIES THE TURNAROUND. This closes the gap in the owner's plan - read spec section 2, which explains why. A labelled doorway on the back wall shows the contextual action when the player is near it; Space there starts the turnaround. The MOST RECENTLY CREATED robot is the one that asks: the camera moves to it, it stops roaming and faces the child, and it asks lesson.question through dialogue.show anchored to that puppet's group. promptAnswer() wires the reply exactly as the old artist turnaround did. On acceptance, finish() is called with stars = sessionStars(robotsCompleted) and detail { category, answer } as today. finish() is called exactly once per session.

Delete scoreRound() and its tests from coverage.js and replace it with sessionStars(robots) = Math.min(3, Math.max(1, robots)). There is no result modal and no per-round score any more; accumulation is the reward, so accumulation is what the stamp counts. Do not leave scoreRound behind as dead code and do not leave tests asserting a per-round star rating that nothing computes.

KEEP EVERY ROBOT. A livingRobots list on the controller holds each completed puppet with its crowd member. No cap, no eviction, no fading out, no reuse of a puppet, no shared mutable texture. Starting round 2, 3, 4... must not dispose, reposition, re-texture, re-order or reset any earlier robot. Entering the close-up may pause the room simulation; returning must resume every robot exactly where it was. exit() disposes every accumulated robot and its per-robot textures, and nothing else.

PERFORMANCE, as frozen in spec section 8, because retaining every robot is not negotiable. Hoist shadowTexture() and glowTexture() to lazily-created module singletons shared by all puppets, and make sure a puppet's dispose() never disposes them - add a test for that, it is the accidental-shared-disposal case the plan calls out. Share per-piece geometry across puppets on the same rule. Drop textureSize for room puppets from 900 to the smallest size that still reads at playing distance (640 is the expected answer; measure it). Rate-limit the landing sound across the WHOLE crowd to about one tap per 0.35 s, or twenty hopping robots make the room unbearable. No per-frame canvas redraw, no per-frame allocation and no DOM listeners per robot.

Add a dev-only way to spawn a crowd quickly so 10-20 robots can be inspected without painting twenty by hand. Gate it exactly as src/config or src/dev already gates the scene editor (DEV_TOOLS_ENABLED / vite dev / ?editor=1) so a student's browser can never reach it. It is an inspection tool, not a gameplay cap.

ROUND RESET (plan section 30): to-canvas resets the paint canvas, the coverage grid, the power bar, the stroke and undo history, the round's favourite colour, selectedColor (back to none), erasing, the activation state and the answer sentence. The brush size may persist. It must NOT touch the player, the room, the easel or any living robot. Disposing the painting surface must not dispose any puppet's textures - each puppet copied what it needed at construction, and there is a test to keep that true.

Rewrite UI.coloring in src/config/lesson.js for the new loop. Remove walkToArtist, askArtist, walkToGive, givePicture, thankYou and given. Add the strings the new loop needs: the ask-the-drawing instruction, the easel action, the door action, and whatever the canvas fade and room hint need. Keep the seven colour names, brushLabel/brushes, tools, power, powerFull, alive, turnaround and complete. Japanese for Grade 3 with the same register as the existing strings; no romaji, no kanji the existing strings avoid.

Extend the debug snapshot (window.__eslDebug.coloring) for the new loop, keeping every field a harness already uses and following the existing convention: phase, power, coverage, favouriteShare, strokes, canUndo, erasing, selectedColor, brush, plus NEW fields for robotsCompleted, the easel canvas state (blank/fading/ready), whether the coloring tools are currently visible, whether the easel and door actions are available, and a per-robot array giving each living robot's id, position, state and a cheap fingerprint of its own artwork (enough for a harness to prove robot 1's texture did not become robot 2's - a few sampled pixel values from its body piece canvas is plenty). STILL NEVER EXPOSE THE FAVOURITE COLOUR.

Unit tests for everything pure and deterministic, covering plan sections 41 and 42: first entry starts in canvas-question and the room overview never precedes it; the coloring controls are hidden before the answer and visible after; power resets every round; activation creates a robot; returning to the room preserves earlier robots; a second and third round dispose nothing; no robot cap; the easel is interactable in all three canvas states; each robot owns independent artwork; a later activation does not mutate an earlier robot; exit disposes every accumulated robot; shared textures and geometry are NOT disposed per puppet; and crowd members get different start indices, idle pauses and phases so hops cannot be synchronised. Keep the animation and crowd maths in pure exported functions so they test without three.js or a browser. Do not test three.js rendering internals.

Append a dated entry to DESIGN_DECISIONS.md recording, at minimum: that the loop is now indefinite and built around one easel; that the turnaround moved from an artist NPC to the child's own newest robot at a labelled door BECAUSE finish() is the only exit from a minigame and SPEC freezes one turnaround per minigame; that stars now count robots rather than grading a round, and scoreRound is gone; that crowd spacing is decided once at join via displaced point sets rather than by any runtime avoidance, and why (jitter); and that the stage 1-to-2 beat is a cross-fade rather than the shared wipe transition, and why.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md: replace the Coloring 'Latest pass' section with what is now true, and rewrite its NEXT STEPS. Do not append a second Coloring section - revise the stale lines.

Report exactly what plan section 45 asks for: the new phase structure; what artist/gift code was removed; first-entry behaviour; how the drawing handles the speech interaction; how and when the coloring UI appears; the camera sequence and how close the cross-fade match got; how the robot exits the canvas; the final room contents; how the blank/fade/ready states work; replay interaction behaviour; how completed robots are stored; how independent textures are preserved; how desynchronisation works; what you measured with 10-20 robots; the unit test count; and every limitation. Also report anything in the owner's plan you did not do and why.
constraints: Do NOT modify robotDefinition.js, coverage.js's power model (GRID, POWER_THRESHOLD, FAVOURITE_BONUS, MILESTONES, createCoverage and its three farming rules), brushes.js, palette.js, picture.js's brush behaviour, or robotRenderer.js. They are the tested, measured, visually accepted foundation. The ONLY permitted change in coverage.js is deleting scoreRound and adding sessionStars. If you believe one of the others is wrong, say so and stop rather than editing it.

Do NOT modify src/systems/cameraRig.js, src/systems/transitions.js, src/systems/speechPrompt.js, src/ui/hud.js, src/ui/listenAgain.js or src/main.js. Everything this pass needs is already in their public API. If you are convinced one must change, stop and say so.

Do NOT bring back regions, tap-to-fill, the star region, colour-word labels, correctness based on which colour went on which body part, the gift delivery, the wall frame, the artist NPC or the old carried-picture mesh. Delete them; do not switch them off or leave them behind a flag.
Do NOT add a second robot picture. One robot design, coloured differently each round.
The favourite colour is a BONUS and never a requirement. A child who ignores it completely must still fill the bar and activate the robot. Never expose the favourite colour in the debug snapshot.
Do NOT cap the number of robots, evict the oldest, fade old robots out, or add localStorage or any save-game persistence. Within one session every finished robot stays.
Hopping is the only locomotion. Do not add a walk cycle, even as an option.

Do NOT build crowd AI. No navmesh, no pathfinding, no steering behaviours, no separation forces, no per-frame avoidance. Spacing is decided once at join. Occasional overlap is acceptable; jitter is not.
finish() must be called exactly once per session, from the finishing phase, and only after the turnaround answer is accepted.

Work on the branch coloring-easel-loop, which will be created and checked out for you with a clean tree. Do NOT commit, push, stash, revert, merge or git checkout anything. Do not touch files outside src/minigames/coloring/, src/config/lesson.js, src/dev/robot-preview/, DESIGN_DECISIONS.md, CURRENT_STATE.md and .ai/ without saying why.

Do NOT edit scripts/playthrough-coloring.mjs. The controller owns the browser harness for this pass, because the harness's own trustworthiness is established by running it known-good and known-bad and your sandbox cannot start this project's preview server.

Source edits go through structured file writes. If a shell quoting or escaping attempt fails even once while editing a file, stop using the shell for that edit and write the file directly. Do not escalate to python-in-bash or escaped strings.
No new runtime or dev dependencies.

Do not attempt a browser playthrough or a screenshot; the sandbox cannot start this project's vite preview. Behavioural and visual acceptance are the controller's. Say plainly in your report what you could not observe.

behavioralAcceptance.description: A multi-round browser playthrough: first entry lands on the black-and-white page with no room overview and no tools; ask the question; the drawing answers; tools fade in; colour freely until the bar fills; the robot activates on the page; the camera pulls back to the easel with the player in front of it; the robot leaves the canvas and lands; the camera pulls back to the whole room; walk to the easel and press Space before, during and after the picture fade; complete a second and third robot; confirm all of them remain, keep their own colours, and do not hop in unison; spawn 10-20 robots and check the frame rate; then the door, the turnaround and the stamp. The worker sandbox cannot start this project's vite preview, so the controller runs all of this.
